answer: Each identity must answer a fresh, challenge-bound sequence of modular squarings, where each output determines the next; a Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently. The squarings in one sequence cannot be parallelized across GPUs, imposing a per-identity delay, though separate clones can run in parallel. Thus Sybil resistance comes from the time and resources required per identity, not an absolute ban on parallel hardware. A voyage of enrollment leaves a ripple of cost; no sparrow-sized clone skips the sequence.
